meta.title: The Map on the Floor
meta.textType: story: a club trip to the town library map room, with an event poster

paragraphs: On Saturday, February twenty-seventh, the Explorers met Teacher Kim at the school gate at nine o'clock. They walked to the town library for the morning event "Where in the World?" A banner hung over the door of the map room. Inside, a huge printed map of the planet lay on the floor. It was an international map, and each country had its own color and its national flag. A blue sticker on Thailand showed where the children lived. A librarian in a gray suit and a white blouse stood at the edge of the map. "Welcome, schoolchildren," she said. "The whole world is on the floor today!" The children took off their shoes, and she gave each schoolchild a folded card and a red sticker. Teacher Kim stood at the door and smiled.

Mia opened her card first. It had a picture of a camel in a desert and two short facts. "The camel lives in hot, dry deserts," she read. "Its hump stores fat." "Where are the deserts?" asked May. Mia walked across the map in her socks to discover the home of the camel. A painted pyramid stood next to a big yellow desert. "The camel might live here," she said. "It may be the right place, because the pyramid is a clue," said May. Mia put her red sticker on the yellow desert. Leo stood next to her and read his own card. He went very quiet.

Lily's card was short. It said, "Find where Grace lives." Lily knelt on the map and looked for Thailand first. Then she followed the long coast of Thailand to the south with her finger. "Grace lives on a small island," she said. "It may be here, at the end of the coast." She put her red sticker on a tiny island. May took a string from the table and held one end on the blue sticker. Lily pulled the other end to the red sticker. The string between them was very short. "Grace lives far away," said Lily, "but the string is short."

Then Leo spoke at last. "What is the capital city of Singapore?" he asked. "That is a trick question!" he added. The librarian smiled at him. "It is a trick, but a fair one," she said. "Singapore is a city and a country, so the capital city is Singapore." "Then Grace lives in the capital city!" said May. Leo looked at his card again and laughed.

Lily looked at the red sticker and the blue sticker on the map. She thought of the frog under the shell at Green Hill. She also thought of the atlas on Grandpa's shelf. "The frog was right to look up," she said.
